_rejected_near_misses._why_rejected: the dict variants carry an English gloss that does not fit the prototype's 30px-high 2-column toggle grid and is not the prototype's copy (§0 rule 1). The mobile short forms are minted instead — the B-061 'near-miss labels = new verbatim keys' precedent.
_rejected_near_misses.pm.resultNone: 'ยังไม่ตรวจ' is byte-exact with MPM_RESULTS[0] (L93) but that label is DEAD CODE in the prototype (the `const r` on L109 is never rendered and the toggles are MPM_RESULTS.slice(1)), so the screen needs no 'none' label at all — nothing minted, nothing reused.
_rejected_near_misses.pm.checkProgress: '{n}/{count} รายการ' — the same counter, but the prototype's eyebrow reads 'ตรวจแล้ว n/total' (L105); the verbatim composite is minted instead.
_rejected_near_misses.pm.checklistTitle: 'Checklist ตรวจเช็ค' — the web PM section title; the mobile prototype's header reads 'Checklist PM' (L105).

_composite_tokens: 'progress' carries {n} (checked) and {count} (total). The token NAMES follow the repo convention and are borrowed from dict pm.confirmIncomplete ('ตรวจแล้ว {n}/{count} — …'), which counts exactly the same thing; the prototype writes them as JS ${done}/${items.length}. The screen substitutes via JuneflowI18n.format. A translation MUST keep both tokens (asserted by the sidecar test).
